title: COR1M concentration measure & over-bulled hedge trigger

questions.prompt: Confirm the persona panel that will run this research loop.
questions.description: research_loop.yml currently has personas: [] (must be confirmed per goal). Sample personas already exist at .claude/personas/: cio.md, quant.md, portfolio-manager.md. The loop reviews every finding through this panel.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Confirm all three: CIO, Quant Analyst, Portfolio Manager — they map 1:1 to the shipped persona files and give the macro/rigor/risk-budget lenses this question needs.

questions.prompt: Which claims should become the seed hypotheses (H-COR-001…)?
questions.description: These become the goal's facts and the loop's starting hypotheses. The request splits naturally into a measurement claim and a tradeability claim; a third tests whether COR1M beats a plain vol baseline.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All three. (1) COR1M validly captures extreme single-stock concentration/crowding (measurement validity). (2) The low <8 'over-bulled' tail is a usable forward hedge trigger for equity indices (tradeability). (3) The COR1M tail adds value beyond a VIX/vol-based trigger (incremental edge).

options.label: H1: COR1M validly measures extreme concentration / crowding
H2: COR1M <8 tail is a usable forward hedge trigger
H3: COR1M tail adds edge beyond a VIX/vol baseline

questions.prompt: How should the 'over-bulled' trigger be defined for testing?
questions.description: SpotGamma uses an absolute level. The quant persona will demand a calibration window + quantile basis, so a percentile/z-score variant is the robustness counterpart to the absolute level.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Primary: absolute COR1M < 8 (SpotGamma 'certain risk flag'), with < 9 as a secondary/warning band. Robustness: trailing-percentile (e.g. bottom 5% of a rolling window) and a z-score band, so the trigger isn't anchored to one hard-coded number.

options.label: Z-score / std-dev band vs rolling mean

questions.prompt: Which equity indices should the hedge trigger be evaluated against?
questions.description: Local data has SPY, QQQ, IWM, VIX OHLC. COR1M is S&P-derived, so SPY is the natural home; QQQ/IWM test whether the concentration signal travels to tech-heavy and small-cap indices.
questions.recommendedAnswer: All three available ETFs: SPY (primary, since COR1M is S&P-derived), plus QQQ and IWM to test transfer. VIX is used as the comparison/benchmark signal, not a hedge target.

questions.prompt: What makes the trigger 'usable'? Pick the success metrics and forward horizons.
questions.description: Needs to be testable per the fact sheet. The PM cares about drawdown/risk-budget payoff; the quant cares about hit-rate vs the unconditional base rate and stability across horizons.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Forward max-drawdown elevated vs the unconditional base rate, plus the forward return distribution, measured at 5/10/21/42 trading-day horizons, scored by hit-rate / precision against the base rate (not just average). 'Usable' = a statistically and economically meaningful skew toward downside after the trigger fires.

options.label: Forward max drawdown vs base rate
Hit-rate / precision vs unconditional base rate
Signal lead time before drawdown onset

questions.prompt: Should the loop model the actual hedge instrument, or just the signal on the underlying?
questions.description: Validating the signal (forward index return/drawdown) is separable from structuring a live hedge (put spreads / VIX calls via hedge-convexity-scout). Doing both at once risks conflating signal quality with instrument selection.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Signal-only for the core loop (forward index return/drawdown on the underlying); defer option/convexity structuring to a follow-up experiment once the signal is shown to have edge. Keeps H2 a clean test of the trigger, not of option selection.

options.label: Signal-only on the underlying; option overlay deferred to follow-up
Include an option/convexity overlay from round 1

questions.prompt: How should the 'COR1M measures concentration' claim (H1) be validated, given local data limits?
questions.description: We only have COR1M + index/VIX OHLC locally — no top-N market-cap weight, dispersion, or single-stock call-volume series. This is a real data-availability constraint on H1.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Round 1: treat COR1M's construction as the concentration proxy and cross-check against what's available (VIX, realized index correlation/dispersion derivable from the ETFs). Flag external concentration ground-truth (top-N weight, single-stock call volume) as a follow-up experiment to fetch only if H1 needs it — don't block the tradeability work on it.

options.label: Use COR1M as proxy + available cross-checks; external data is a follow-up
Require external concentration data now (adds a data dependency)
Defer H1 entirely; round 1 is tradeability-only

questions.prompt: Confirm the round cap and what is explicitly OUT of scope.
questions.description: research_loop.yml sets round_cap: 3 (a deliberate stopping point, ends in a decision-maker memo). Scope guardrails keep the loop from drifting into productionization.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep round cap = 3. Out of scope: live execution / broker integration, intraday/tick data, non-equity assets, a full backtest/portfolio engine, and parameter over-optimization (curve-fitting the threshold). The deliverable is an evidence-backed verdict + decision memo, not a deployed strategy.
